en: but the way things are, it's just
note: Continues slice 053 #4319 'With more money I could buy a new boat,' (lower case).

en: hopeless, isn't it
Maybe I should go borrow money from the bank
I guess a business needs investment first.
Thinking I could earn by fixing up cheap boats,
that was naive of me, wasn't it.
Huh? Who are you?
Is it about a boat?
Oh, I guess not. Bye, then.
I'm busy right now. Sorry.
Oh, it's you. Hello.
I'd rather you came to my work at noon,
not here. That would suit me better.
Why not take a boat out while you're here?
Hello. How are things with you?
Not so great on my end.
But I'll manage somehow.
No use getting discouraged, after all.
I need the money.
Rather than toil at work that earns you nothing,
I shall offer you a better choice...
Become my servant.
Now your power surpasses any human's.
From now on, fretting over such petty things
is something you would do well to give up.
Yes, it is. By the way
that's quite a big load you're carrying.
I see, so that's what it is.
Good luck with your work.
Boats? What line of work are you in?
No, I'm sorry, but I was only passing
by. No boat for me, thank you.
Yes, one of these days.
(Out of the question! Me, go near a river...)
What's the matter? You look down.
, my master. Your orders...
I dreamt I was wandering the streets at night.
I'm hardly at the age for nights on the town...
Command me as you will...
note: After #854 ', my master.' (new sentence) and after #4430 (Wilfred, slice 055).

en: I've got a bruise on my back.
Trouble is, I can't treat my own back.
Oh, what's wrong? Here to see the doctor?
You look pale. Does it hurt anywhere?
No. I am sturdier than I look.
Really? Somehow you still look a bit
under the weather to me.
I'm Quentin, a physician.
Come by whenever you feel unwell.
We're only human. Don't overdo it.
(As if one such as I could ever fall ill.)
Are you coming down with a cold or something?
You do look pale, you know.
You still look rather pale. What do you say,
shall I examine you while you're here?
No, thank you.
Talking with you is one thing, but
I have never cared for hospitals.
Is that so? Ha ha ha ha.
But that won't do.
You'll ruin your health one day.
Good of you to come. Hello.
Hmm, you seem to be in good health, so
you must just be pale by nature.
I may have troubled you by pushing
an examination on you. Forgive me.
Though I think most doctors would make
the same mistake.
Are you keeping well?
There's a cold going around London lately.
Do take care of yourself.
Lately more people in town are looking pale.
Whatever could be the matter...
You're white as a sheet! An emergency?
I'll see emergencies at any hour.
No, it seems I have come to the wrong place.
(...Doctors are not much to my liking.)
Come to me whenever you're feeling unwell.
Oh, hello. How are you feeling?
More people have been looking poorly lately.
They turn pale and sleep all day.
